this day, the court made the following:
 Order
This writ petition is filed seeking quashing the notice dated 22.12.2012 issued by the fifth respondent at Annexure-D and for mandamus to consider the application filed to the second respondent.

2. The case of the petitioner is that he has obtained permission from the fourth respondent to carry on the industry of manufacturer of packaged drinking water in the name and style as Balaji Products.
He has invested huge amount, engaged the employees and purchased the vehicles to transport.
He has got tested the water from the concerned authorities.
The fifth respondent issued notice dated 22.12.2012, to the petitioner asking him to produce the ISI certificate or applied acknowledgment.
He has applied for ISI (BSI) certificate on 11.01.2013 by submitting relevant documents and paying requisite fee.
The said request is yet to be considered.
In the meanwhile on 23.1.2013 the first respondent issued one more notice asking him to close the business, otherwise they have threaten to disconnect the electricity supply.
Therefore petitioner approached before this Court.

In similar matter in the batch of cases in W.P.No.100504-100508/2013 & W.P.No.100516/ 2013,
the following observations are made in para 3.

It reads as under;
"3. The question which is involved in this writ petition was the subject matter of batch of writ petitions before the Principal Bench in W.P.No.17713/2012 and other connected matters.

Those batch of writ petitions were disposed of on 09.11.2012 by common order, the operative portion of which reads as under:
ORDER 1. Writ Petition No.17713/2012 is allowed in part.

2. W.P.Nos.17467-17498/2012 and W.P.Nos.
24257-283/2012 are hereby disposed of.

3. The respondent authorities are hereby directed to ensure that all necessary steps are taken to prohibit, prevent the manufacture and sale of packaged drinking water without certification from the Bureau of Indian Standards.

4. The respondent authorities are hereby directed to take action against the manufacturers of packaged drinking water if found to be running the units without certification from the Bureau of Indian Standards.

5. The manufacturers of packaged drinking water shall submit application as prescribed under the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 and the Regulations made thereunder and as provided under Manojkumar S/O Kishore Bhai vs Union Of India & Ors on 22 February, 2013 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/75940118/
3 the Bureau of India Standards Act, 1986 for issuance of certification from the Bureau of Indian Standards for manufacture, sale or exhibition of packaged drinking water within 15 days from today.

sentences.text:
6. On such submission of application by the manufacturers the authorities concerned shall process the said applications within three months from the date of submission of such applications and notify the deficiency if any to be complied by such manufacturers by fixing such time as the authority may so decide taking into consideration the exigencies and not beyond four months.
7.

The authorities shall dispose of the said applications submitted by the manufacturers accordingly keeping the time limit fixed herein above and if any of the manufacturers fail to comply with the directions or conditions imposed by the authorities to bring their units to the standards prescribed under the Act and Regulations, they will be at liberty to proceed in accordance with law.
Accordingly, this petition also allowed in like terms.

It is made clear that if the applications already filed by the petitioner is not in the prescribed form, the petitioner shall file one more set of applications in the prescribed form along with all requisite documents within a week from today.
Thereafter the respondents shall dispose of the said applications on or before the end of June 2013.
Till such time the respondents shall not interfere with the business of the petitioners.
The learned Government Advocate and the Advocate for Central Government is permitted to file memo of appearance within four weeks.
